definitions.gloss: distant view; looking far away; gazing into the distance
definitions.explanation: The act of looking at something far away, or the view itself seen from a distance. A literary and descriptive word often used for scenic landscapes.

examples.japanese: {山|やま}の{上|うえ}から{海|うみ}を{遠望|えんぼう}する。
examples.english: To gaze at the sea from the mountaintop.

examples.japanese: {遠望|えんぼう}すると、{富士山|ふじさん}の{姿|すがた}が{見|み}えた。
examples.english: Looking into the distance, I could see the shape of Mt. Fuji.

examples.japanese: {展望台|てんぼうだい}からは、{晴|は}れた{日|ひ}には{遠|とお}くの{島々|しまじま}まで{遠望|えんぼう}できる。
examples.english: From the observation deck, you can see distant islands on clear days.

notes:
Composed of {遠|えん} (far, distant) and {望|ぼう} (to gaze, to hope). A somewhat literary word used in descriptive writing, travel guides, and scenic descriptions. Also functions as a する verb: {遠望|えんぼう}する (to gaze into the distance).

USAGE:
Often appears in travel writing, photography descriptions, and literary prose. More evocative and formal than simply {遠|とお}くを{見|み}る (to look far away).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {遠望|えんぼう}する — to gaze into the distance
- {遠望|えんぼう}できる — can be seen from afar
- {山|やま}を{遠望|えんぼう}する — to view a mountain from the distance

RELATED WORDS:
- {展望|てんぼう} — panoramic view; broader, often from an elevated vantage point
- {眺望|ちょうぼう} — view, prospect; similar but emphasizes the scenery being viewed
- {望遠|ぼうえん} — telephoto, far-seeing; same kanji reversed, used in {望遠|ぼうえん}レンズ (telephoto lens)
